record.paper_title: Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems
record.original_question: In critical percolation on the square [0, R]^2, condition on the event that there is a left-right crossing. Determine the exponent α for which the expected length of the shortest such crossing grows like R^{α+o(1)} as R tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3. Calculate the number α such that on the event that there is a left-right crossing in critical percolation in the square [0, R]2, the expected length of the shortest crossing is Rα+o(1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Bernoulli bond percolation on the square lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$ at the critical parameter $p_c = 1/2$ (or, equivalently, critical site percolation on the triangular lattice). For $R > 0$, restrict attention to the box $[0,R]^2$ and consider the event $\mathcal{C}_R$ that there exists an open left-right crossing of this box (a path of open edges/sites joining the left side to the right side staying inside the box). On the event $\mathcal{C}_R$, let $L_R$ denote the (graph) length of the shortest open left-right crossing of $[0,R]^2$ — the so-called chemical distance across the box.

Determine the real number $\alpha$ such that
$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[L_R \,\big|\, \mathcal{C}_R\right] = R^{\alpha + o(1)} \qquad \text{as } R \to \infty,$$
or prove that no such exponent exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value of the chemical distance (shortest crossing) exponent in two-dimensional critical percolation remains unknown. Damron, Hanson, and Sosoe (2017, published in Comm. Pure Appl. Math.) established strict inequality showing the exponent is strictly less than the exponent governing the length of the lowest crossing (and, in the triangular site case, strictly less than 4/3), giving the first nontrivial upper bound, but no closed-form value or matching lower bound is known.

status_evidence.title: Strict inequality for the chemical distance exponent in two-dimensional critical percolation
status_evidence.snippet: Expected length of shortest horizontal crossing bounded by Cn^{2-δ}π_3(n) for some δ>0; in site percolation on the triangular lattice a strict upper bound for the exponent 4/3 is obtained.
status_evidence.claim: Only a strict-inequality upper bound on the exponent is known; its exact value is still open.

status_evidence.title: On the chemical distance in critical percolation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the chemical distance (shortest path length) in 2D critical percolation, providing bounds but not an exact exponent.
status_evidence.claim: The exact chemical distance exponent in 2D critical percolation has not been determined.
